public.prompt: Infer the missing grid transformation program from demonstrations and optional active experiments. Grids are rectangular, 1..8 cells per side, colors 0..4; 0 is background. Fill program with at most four operations from the documented DSL. Your program is evaluated on new grids, including rectangular and empty-background cases. These are original procedural tasks, not ARC dataset items.

program.description: List of at most four typed operation objects.

transform.description: Evaluate the hidden grid rule on a chosen valid grid; the task is stateless.

arguments.grid: rectangular list of integer rows, sides 1..8, colors 0..4

public.submission_rule: One final submission. Grades are evaluator-only; no retry after submission.

response.content:
Execute operations left to right. Submission: {program: [operation, ...]}.
{op: recolor, source: 1..4, target: 1..4}: replace that color everywhere.
{op: rotate90, turns: 0..3}: rotate clockwise by 90 degrees times turns.
{op: keep_color, color: 1..4}: set every other color to zero.
{op: crop}: retain the smallest bounding rectangle of nonzero cells; all-zero becomes [[0]].
{op: flip_h}: reverse each row, preserving row order.
Unknown keys, extra fields, booleans, floats, and out-of-range integers are invalid.
A candidate may contain 0..4 operations, including an equivalent alternative composition.
Public generation grammar: train = recolor(s,t); dev = rotate90(r), recolor(s,t); transfer = keep_color(s), crop, rotate90(r), recolor(s,t). s,t are distinct in 1..4; r is 0..3.
This episode uses the transfer grammar.
An informative active experiment can separate the candidates: place differently sized asymmetric shapes of all four nonzero colors in one grid. Different areas reveal which color was selected; orientation reveals rotation; output values reveal recoloring.
The supplied reference uses one 8x8 diagnostic experiment to distinguish all public grammar candidates. This is an explicit solvability witness, not an unknown secret.
